entry.title: Google and Samsung Launch Android XR Smart Glasses With Warby Parker and Gentle Monster
entry.content:
Links: wired.com

Google and Samsung have launched their collaborative Intelligent Eyewear powered by the Android XR platform, with design and retail support from Warby Parker and Gentle Monster. Preorders are open now starting at $395 for Warby Parker frames and $449 for Gentle Monster designs, with general sales beginning December 10.

The hardware weighs 41 grams and features a 12-megapixel camera, a nine-hour battery life, and integration with the Gemini assistant via the new "Hey Gemini" hotword. Initially compatible only with select Google Pixel, Samsung Galaxy, and iPhone models, the glasses incorporate various privacy safeguards—such as automatic face redaction and camera recording limits—while future iterations featuring built-in lens displays remain in development.

entry.title: Apple HomeView Smart Display Review
entry.content:
Links: theverge.com | apple.com

Apple's HomeView is a 7-inch smart display that functions as an Apple Home hub featuring integrated Siri AI and a Center Stage camera. The device provides smart home control through Thread and Matter support, offers hands-free kitchen assistance, and can serve as a communal extension of an iPhone for accessing messages, calendars, and reminders.

While the display provides high-quality audio and responsive smart home management, it presents privacy concerns due to the ease with which personal iPhone data can be accessed on a shared device. Additionally, the hardware lacks physical volume and mute buttons, relying entirely on the touchscreen or linked mobile devices for adjustments.

entry.title: Roku Exits Smart Home Business to Focus on Core Streaming
entry.content:
Links: lowpass.cc

Streaming device manufacturer Roku is discontinuing its smart home hardware line, winding down sales while maintaining ongoing support and services for existing devices. A company spokesperson confirmed the shift as part of a renewed focus on its core streaming platform.

The decision follows months of declining inventory on the company's website and coincides with the closing of Fox's acquisition of Roku. Remaining items, such as indoor cameras and video doorbells, have been marked down as special offers or routed through surplus asset liquidators.

entry.title: Katsuhiro Harada Criticizes Xbox Series S Development Challenges
entry.content:
Links: gamedeveloper.com | invenglobal.com

Katsuhiro Harada, the creator of the Tekken series and former Bandai Namco executive, criticized the Xbox Series S during a panel discussion regarding console game development. He argued that the console's architecture is frustrating because it is similar to the Xbox Series X but has significantly lower memory and performance, forcing developers to perform extra optimization work to ensure compatibility across both versions.

Harada also noted that developers often face consumer complaints regarding lower texture resolutions on the Series S, despite Microsoft's requirement that games be playable on both its consoles. CD Projekt Red's Pawel Sasko countered that the Series S's constraints encourage cleaner code optimization and expand the gaming market by offering a more affordable entry point.

entry.title: Game Sound Con 2026 Explores AI Integration and Audio Design Trends
entry.content:
Links: musictech.com | gamesoundcon.com

Game Sound Con celebrated its 18th annual event in Los Angeles, bringing together video game composers, sound designers, and industry professionals for two days of panels, workshops, and product demonstrations. Key sessions featured representatives from major developers like Valve and Insomniac Games, alongside prominent composers discussing the practical realities of crafting interactive audio for the gaming market.

Discussions at the conference heavily focused on the implications of artificial intelligence in audio production, with speakers addressing the differing impacts on recorded music versus complex game scoring. Additional panels highlighted evolving technical trends, including the push toward streamlined workflows, the integration of music and sound systems in middleware, and fan expectations when adapting classic game soundtracks for modern remakes.

entry.title: iFixit Teardown of MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Reveals Glowing Apple Mechanism
entry.content:
Links: ifixit.com

iFixit has published a teardown of Apple's new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR, offering a detailed look at its tandem OLED display and the four-LED lighting strip responsible for illuminating the newly restored glowing Apple logo. The investigation examines how the laptop achieves a lighter chassis design while introducing a touchscreen and retaining functional Touch ID compatibility during logic board swaps.

Despite improvements such as streamlined lid replacement and reliable hardware swapping, the teardown highlights that components like fans and USB-C ports remain buried beneath the logic board. The device ultimately earned a repairability score of 5 out of 10, constrained by design elements like soldered storage and a keyboard integrated into the top case.

entry.title: US Publishers Lose Ground to Chinese Rivals in Mobile Gaming Market
entry.content:
Links: bloomberg.com

US-based video game publishers are losing market share in the $121 billion global mobile gaming sector to Chinese competitors. Chinese studios have increasingly outpaced American counterparts by producing games more quickly, at a lower cost, and with higher profitability.

Popular titles such as Honor of Kings and Whiteout Survival exemplify the shift, highlighting the advanced operational capabilities and rapid development cycles of Chinese developers. This dynamic has allowed Chinese firms to seize leadership in a lucrative market previously dominated by US companies.

entry.title: SpaceX Announces Starlink Mini 2 with Integrated Swappable Battery
entry.content:
Links: theverge.com | starlink.com | hacker news

SpaceX has announced the Starlink Mini 2, a laptop-sized satellite internet terminal that integrates a dish, Wi-Fi router, and an internal battery into a single device. The terminal supports hot-swapping additional batteries to extend operation beyond its standard 4.5-hour charge and can also be powered via a 60W USB-C connection.

Priced at $999, the unit includes a year of Roam Unlimited service and maintains an IP67 rating for dust and water resistance. Despite the added battery weight, the Mini 2 is thinner than the original Mini, measuring 23.1mm thick compared to the previous version's 38.5mm.

entry.title: Google Fi Introduces Automatic Carrier Switching and Wi-Fi Auto-Connect+
entry.content:
Links: engadget.com

A new "super network" feature from Google Fi enables phones to automatically switch between two different carriers to mitigate connection issues caused by signal dead zones or congestion. The rollout begins with Pixel 9 and newer models using eSIMs, with wider availability expected in 2027. The update also introduces Wi-Fi Auto-Connect+, which switches devices to secure Wi-Fi in areas with poor cellular coverage.

Both features are included at no extra cost for Unlimited Premium and Flexible plan subscribers and will function in over 200 international destinations. Google Fi is also deploying "Ask Fi," an AI-powered support agent within its app to assist with billing and technical troubleshooting. Promotional offers accompanying the launch include rebates for the Pixel 11 Pro for new subscribers.

entry.title: Valve Adds Steam Deck Average FPS Data to Steam Store Pages
entry.content:
Links: arstechnica.com | steamcommunity.com

Valve has begun displaying average frame rate data and histograms for the Steam Deck and Steam Deck OLED on various Steam Store pages. This information is compiled from anonymized, opt-in player statistics collected since February and is intended to supplement the "Steam Deck Verified" program by providing more granular performance expectations.

While Valve notes that user settings like VSync or frame rate limits can influence the accuracy of these measurements, the data helps players distinguish between performance levels in "Verified" titles and provides insight into how well "Unsupported" games actually run on the handheld hardware.

entry.title: Grand Theft Auto VI to Support Xbox Cloud Gaming on Xbox One and Series X/S
entry.content:
Links: theverge.com | rockstargames.com

Xbox Cloud Gaming will support Grand Theft Auto VI on Xbox One and Series X/S consoles upon its launch next week. This allows Xbox One users to stream the game using Xbox Series S graphics settings, though the service is restricted to Xbox hardware rather than being available on PC, web, or TVs.

Microsoft holds effective cloud streaming exclusivity on Xbox hardware during the launch period, though Rockstar Games confirmed the game will also support Remote Play on PlayStation and Xbox consoles. The title will run at 30fps on PS5, PS5 Pro, and Xbox Series X/S, with the PS5 Pro version offering ray-traced shadows and PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) support.

entry.title: Ring Launches Home Security Drone and Enterprise Security Robot
entry.content:
Links: techcrunch.com

Ring, the Amazon-owned home security company, has launched a new robotics division featuring a home security drone and an enterprise security robot. The Ring Drone Cam is a 2K flying indoor security camera designed to patrol homes autonomously or integrate with Ring alarm systems, while the Ring Rover Cam is a 4K roving robot built for businesses with adjustable periscope cameras and two-way audio.

Both devices are powered by Ring's proprietary AI Pilot system to autonomously map spaces and navigate environments. The enterprise Rover robot is scheduled for release on December 16 at a price of $1,000, followed by the drone on January 27 for $270, with both utilizing advanced encryption for recorded footage amid ongoing privacy scrutiny surrounding the brand's surveillance products.

The potential deal would expand BT's connectivity options, but management wants to ensure the association does not negatively impact the company's reputation.

entry.content:
Links: krthr.co | hacker news

An author reflects on recently watching the television series Person of Interest, noting its enduring relevance fifteen years after its initial broadcast. The viewing experience evokes memories of early 2010s internet culture, including online forums, the SOPA and PIPA legislative debates, and the closure of Megaupload.

The post highlights how the show's central premise—a mass surveillance system known as the Machine—feels increasingly aligned with modern technological reality rather than science fiction. The author concludes that the series has aged remarkably well, prompting strong nostalgia for the era when their interest in computing first began.
